P01.note: "by the 1980s the processions in all nine villages used the same verses" alone yields harmonized; democratized/dramatized/enshrined are only weakly tempting.

P02.note: Abandonment after handling plus the untouched far boxes fledging most makes intrusive; methodical literally fits the repeated weighing.

P03.note: "By 1880 the county had two codes of football ... a club from one never met a club from the other" gives splintered directly.

P04.note: Launched needs "No legislator, newspaper, or fishing club had ever proposed removing it" combined with the hearings/letters; jolted and legitimized presuppose a prior debate and are near-misses.

P05.note: "almost every new play reminded her of one she had already seen" signals jaded; younger critics' praise kills judicious.

P06.note: The surcharge kept apart plus replacement hulls for losses must be combined to see insurer; "at no charge" kills lender.

P07.note: Upstream's real compliance (kills token) and downstream never answering and continuing (kills tacit) must be combined for unilateral.

P08.note: Contrast of generational variation with 1975 baskets indistinguishable from 1952 gives petrified; professionalized is the main near-miss.

P09.note: "knee-high ... while oaks planted at the same time ... had reached twenty feet" gives dwarfed; "spreading and green" kills defoliated/felled.

P10.note: "a closing verse ... telling young men that a broken oath will find them out at sea" gives moralized outright; the alliterative distractors are weak.

P11.note: "every orchard tree and cornstalk lying in the same direction" gives flattened; "soil the water had barely disturbed" kills gouged and the river back in its bed kills dammed.

P12.note: "He does whatever the last sister to speak with him asks" points to pawn; pivot is defensible since his errands move the quarrel.

P13.note: "Each autumn the harvest went south by the trainload to the city's mills" gives granary; farm-family population kills dormitory.

P14.note: Chance weather on one day doubling or halving shares gives lottery; lever and keystone fit the clause's importance in the first sentence.

P15.note: "a separate claim for each room ... came back unread if one box was blank" gives bureaucratic outright.

P16.note: "families from the lower streets who lodged in it for weeks at a time" during wet springs gives refuge outright.

P17.note: Board closed any hospital that fell short plus the county hospital alone still open, unchanged, gives certified.

P18.note: "she traveled to the capital and the county seat to present those requests and returned with the officials' terms" gives envoy outright.

P19.note: Explaining aloud to see failures plus "never touched the apparatus" (kills apprentice) gives audience.

P20.note: Crews drawn whenever a district fell behind gives reservoir of labor; outpost literally fits a remote eastern district.

P21.note: "sealed each family's goods ... handed them back ... with the seals unbroken" gives custodian; checkpoint literally sits on the pass.

P22.note: "fined on a Tuesday and passed without comment on Friday" and no routes or schedules give haphazard outright.

P23.note: "The outer walls were glass from floor to ceiling ... the staff switched on no lamps" gives airy; murals and trees kill austere.

P24.note: Six hundred measures passing or failing as advised gives rudder; ritual literally fits a weekly fifty-year column.

P25.note: "he paid off its debts and sent her a fixed sum every month" gives benefactor outright.

P26.note: "had to anchor under the port's guns and pay a duty on its cargo" gives tollgate outright.

P27.note: "gave the secretary a vote only when the members were evenly divided" gives tiebreaker outright.

P28.note: Silt settling and dye binding plus gauges showing equal flow in and out (kills sponge) gives sieve/filter.

P29.note: "The composer kept only the first eight bars" of thirty-two gives clipped outright.

P30.note: Buyers walked through before prices plus meetings held elsewhere so nothing looked worn gives showpiece; stone hall tempts stronghold.

P31.note: "the canal dug in 1840 follows his line, and the three villages became the kingdom's chief mill towns" gives prescient.

P32.note: Set days, shared warehouse and single convoy give coordinated; "never bought or sold a sack" and "every dealer still set his own prices" kill cornered.

P33.note: Duty raised to nine days and fine to ten shillings plus laborers who could neither spare nor pay gives onerous; obsolete is the near-miss.

P34.note: "He opened every crate ... down to a missing spoon" gives meticulous outright; incorruptible is unsupported.

P35.note: "dried and separated them one at a time ... copied out nearly every word" gives salvaged outright.

P36.note: Landowner's anti-tenant argument plus demands set against its sentences gives foil; program arranged under its headings makes handbook a strong literal near-miss.

P37.note: "closes with several paragraphs telling the reader what the season should teach" gives didactic outright.

P38.note: "nearly every singer ... sang the record's seven verses to the record's tune" gives standardized outright.

P39.note: Letters mailed to the capital, reprinted, and read at hearings gives megaphone; lens is a near-miss for exposing cheating.

P40.note: Survey confirmed the ridge source but removed the volcano theory that explained it, leaving textbooks without a why; pruned is a close second.
